subject.title: fix(cron): bound cron quarantine sidecar file reads

question: Should cron overflow recovery silently retain only five quarantine archives, or should archive inspection and cleanup be an explicit doctor-owned recovery workflow?
rationale: The code cannot determine how long malformed cron records must remain recoverable; choosing silent deletion versus operator-controlled recovery is a durable product and data-lifecycle policy decision.

options.title: Doctor-owned archive lifecycle
options.body: Keep the size protection, make recovery and cleanup explicit through doctor tooling, and preserve quarantined records until an operator chooses cleanup.

options.title: Approve fixed retention
options.body: Accept silent oldest-first deletion after five archives and document that older quarantined cron rows are not recoverable.

options.title: Defer archive recovery
options.body: Land only the bounded read/write protection and leave overflow recovery fail-closed until a retained-data policy is designed.

recommendation.title: Doctor-owned archive lifecycle
recommendation.body: Keep the size protection, make recovery and cleanup explicit through doctor tooling, and preserve quarantined records until an operator chooses cleanup.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR explicitly routes the archive-retention choice to this decision owner.
